content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: rwd-rt-5 node pool reports repeated OOM/CUDA failures in serving runtime (paged allocator path). 8 pod evictions in last 12m. Affected service: /runtime/serve (text-gen + embeddings). Links: https://dash.redwood/example/incidents/3070001234

alice_oncall: acked - I'm on it. seeing repeated 'cudaErrorLaunchFailure' and 'AllocatorOOM: page allocation failed' in the runtime logs. initial hunch: KV cache pages not being reclaimed -> fragmentation / sticky pages.

alice_oncall: grabbing logs from one of the evicted pods: 
```
[2026-03-15T03:14:02Z] runtime: AllocatorOOM: cannot reserve 512MB for kv-page slab
[2026-03-15T03:14:02Z] runtime: cudaErrorLaunchFailure at kernel attention_paged
[2026-03-15T03:14:02Z] runtime: attempt eviction 0 -> free 0 bytes (frag ratio 0.92)
```

ben_sre: oncall takeover in 10m if you need. I'm pulling node-level metrics and dmesg. Could be a slow leak (creep). Any signs of repeated small allocations never freed?

alice_oncall: yeah heap snapshots show repeated small KV allocations (~64-256B) accumulating in hot slabs. eviction isn't compacting contiguous free ranges. not immediate fix.

kyle_runtime: copy. two quick mitigations to try in parallel: 1) reduce max batch_size to reduce per-request KV pressure; 2) for canary nodes, disable attention-paging fallback so they use resident attention (more memory but less allocator churn). both are config flips, low risk.

maya_support: customer impact check: dashboard shows spike in 500s on embeddings route starting ~03:07Z, 4 customer orgs affected (org-7, org-42, org-88, org-park). CS alerted and drafting a short status note. ETA to notify customers?

alice_oncall: create short blurb: "We're investigating elevated OOMs causing failed requests to embedding endpoints; mitigation in progress. We will update in 30m." Maya assign to CS.

maya_support: created incident-ops -> cs-update draft: "Experiencing higher error rates for embeddings; engineers are mitigating. No data loss. Next update in 30m." pinging nina_product for customer impact prioritization @nina_product

nina_product: thanks, prioritizing org-42 & org-88 for proactive outreach. keep me posted on ETA to restore.

ben_sre: dmesg from rwd-rt-5-07: 
```
[ 1234.567890] rbt: oom_kill_process: Killed process 4123 (rwd-runtime) total-vm: 1536000kB
[ 1234.568001] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
```

ben_sre: starting live mitigations now: scaling node pool +2 (add capacity) and draining one problematic node to rebuild slab layout. deploy-bot, please trigger nodegroup scale-up.

deploy-bot: @ben_sre scaling node group rwd-rt-5 by +2 instances. Estimated 4m to spin up. Rolling restart of pods on rwd-rt-5-07 scheduled after drain.

alice_oncall: also rolling a canary config change to reduce batch_size from 8->4 on 10% of traffic to validate pressure reduction. command: 
```
rwdctl route update --service runtime-serve --setting max_batch_size=4 --traffic 10%
```

kyle_runtime: if fragmentation persists after scale + batch reduction, plan B is to run `kv-compact` on a drained node. note: kv-compact pauses request handling on that node for ~20-40s and will move/refactor pages to reduce fragmentation. example: 
```
./rwdctl runtime kv-compact --node rwd-rt-5-09 --timeout 60s
```

ben_sre: i'll coordinate kv-compact window during low traffic on one node at a time. will also tighten the eviction aggressiveness: set `kv.eviction_threshold` from 0.85 -> 0.7 to force earlier reclamation.

alice_oncall: adding runbook link: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/kv-frag. folks, please record all actions.

maya_support: CS update posted. customers notified for org-42 & org-88.

ben_sre: initial mitigations applied: batch_size canary live, nodegroup scaled, eviction_threshold set to 0.7 on canary nodes. monitoring shows 30% reduction in 500s from canary traffic in the last 3m.

alice_oncall: handoff to ben_sre — I've got to step off for the 30m rotation. Ben — please lead live mitigation and customer comms. I'll sync up after rotation.

ben_sre: taking over. current plan: 1) monitor scale-up; 2) run kv-compact on one drained node if fragmentation metric doesn't drop below 0.6 in 15m; 3) prepare to roll full eviction_threshold change if needed. notifying infra for potential emergency kernel upgrade if NV drivers keep dropping GPUs.

kyle_runtime: FYI, if we kv-compact and fragmentation doesn't improve, we should consider temporary fallback to smaller model variant that uses less KV cache for the affected customer classes. I'll prepare a rollout patch.

ben_sre: noted. tagging incident severity P1 due to multiple customer 500s and repeated node flaps. updating incident tracker. :thumbsup:

alice_oncall: thanks team. leaving detailed notes in the incident tracker and will add timeline after.

nina_product: appreciate the quick coordination. please ping me when stable so we can close CS loop.

incident-bot: Incident updated: owner=ben_sre, severity=P1, mit_status=active_mitigation, next_update=3070002160.

ben_sre: live notes posted to the incident doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/3070001234/notes. continuing monitoring.

maya_support: will follow up on customer callbacks and update the CS tickets.

ben_sre: final quick status at handoff time: error-rate down 45% overall, OOMs reduced after scale + eviction change, but fragmentation still above baseline on two nodes. kv-compact scheduled in 12m for rwd-rt-5-09.

kyle_runtime: I'll join the kv-compact window and watch for regressions. if things look stable after compaction we can consider re-raising eviction_threshold slowly.

ben_sre: closing handoff note. next_update in 20m or earlier if things change. :white_check_mark:
